title: Stand-off intensifies as street protest meets online support

ai.summary: Meghalaya teachers in deficit schools and colleges oppose the state's Centralised Fund Scheme 2026, leading to a sit-in and marches near the Main Secretariat in Shillong as the government insists on proceeding with the Shillong Peak Ropeway project.

facts.claim: Meghalaya teachers in deficit schools and colleges oppose the state's Centralised Fund Scheme 2026
facts.quote: Staff of Meghalaya's deficit schools and colleges reject the state's Centralised Fund Scheme 2026.

facts.claim: The government insists on proceeding with the Shillong Peak Ropeway project
facts.quote: the Meghalaya government has stood firm, declaring that the Rs 151-crore project—targeted for completion by 2028—will not be scrapped.

facts.claim: The project is 3.15 km away from Shillong Peak
facts.quote: the government clarified that a distance of 3.15 km separates the project site from Shillong Peak itself.

ai.background_note: The Meghalaya teachers' strike over the Centralised Fund Scheme 2026 has intensified, with the government maintaining the Shillong Peak Ropeway project despite opposition from the Joint Action Committee.
